text:
Ally: Request: one-page decision aid for webinar follow-up. Audience = platform security + procurement. Must compare Hosted / Dedicated / Private, include two safe benchmark callouts (no raw numbers), and route inbound to a gated intake so SDRs can triage. Keep it single-column and scannable.
Ben: I'll draft. Proposed structure: short headline, three stacked cards (one line benefit + 1-line security note), a 3-row micro-compare (Security | SLA | Typical buyer), a 3-question SDR signal block, and a gated CTA. Use conservative benchmark language: 'low p95 profiles' and 'meaningful unit-cost improvements via batching', link to benchmark hub ID: BENCH-2024-77.
Priya: Security/legal: don't list KMS partners or promise air-gapped turnkey installs. Safe line: 'Configurable networking, KMS integrations, and audit logging.' Add legal footnote: 'Performance varies by model, hardware, and prompt patterns.' Also remove any hard numbers.
Marco: Add a short buyer-signal checklist that maps to lanes: self-serve (Hosted), AE-assisted (Dedicated), Enterprise (Private). Keep triage 3 fields only.
Ops-Bot: Reminder: any benchmark references must cite BENCH-2024-77 and get Ops sign-off before release. Tag @ops in the review step.
Ben: Draft copy below — please reply with quick edits. Intentionally concise for a one-pager layout.

```
Secure inference, made simple: which deployment fits your controls

Hosted — Fastest path to validation
- Benefit: API-first hosted inference for rapid experiments and feature rollouts.
- Security: Shared infra, tenant isolation, RBAC.
- When to pick: prototyping and early product validation.

Dedicated — Predictable capacity & SLAs
- Benefit: Reserved GPU pools and configurable autoscaling for steady production workloads.
- Security: Data-isolated capacity and stronger access controls.
- When to pick: teams needing SLA-backed throughput and predictable latency.

Private — Compliance-first control
- Benefit: VPC or on-prem options with audit logging and customer KMS integrations.
- Security: Network isolation and enterprise policy enforcement.
- When to pick: regulated or highly security-sensitive workloads.

At a glance (Security | SLA | Typical buyer)
- Hosted: Shared controls | Best-effort latency | Product teams/prototypes
- Dedicated: Isolated pools | SLA-backed | Scaling products
- Private: Full control | Configurable SLAs | Regulated enterprises

SDR signal (3 quick fields to capture in the gated form)
- Data residency required? [Yes/No]
- SLA required? [Yes/No]
- Peak throughput band? [Low | Mid | High]

Benchmarks & notes: Refer to BENCH-2024-77 in the benchmark hub for latency profiles by model/region and detailed cost guidance. Performance and unit costs vary by model, hardware, and prompt patterns.

Routing CTA: Book a deployment review (shortlink: redwood.ai/route) — gated intake captures SDR signals and routes to the appropriate sales lane.

Legal: Performance varies by model, hardware, and workload. Contact Sales for on-prem packaging details; options vary by customer.
```

Priya: Please change the throughput bands to explicit CRM buckets: '<2k | 2k-20k | >20k' so SDRs map consistently.
Ben: Updated. Also swapped the shortlink to the gated URL. Will produce PDF tomorrow AM and tag @ops for sign-off.
Marco: Approved on mapping to lanes.
Ops-Bot: Tagging @ops — will review BENCH-2024-77 link before publish.
SDR-Bot: Note: use the three fields to route leads to lanes: Hosted = self-serve, Dedicated = AE + Solutions, Private = Enterprise.
Ally: Owner: Ben. Reviewers: @Priya, @Marco, @ops. Timeline: copy freeze tomorrow AM, final PDF by EOD Friday. Thanks!
